method.commit_match: blob: the target's git blob is in an indexed repository and the chosen commit holds the most of the set's files; closest: the target is in no repository and the commit holding the most set files is recorded; built: the searched commit's build reproduces the contract. method.creation_blocks: eth_getCode is empty at block b-1 and non-empty at block b; the transaction is Blockscout's creation transaction
method.epochs: V3 contracts are not proxies; each holds one code from its creation block to the pinned block, and V3 replaces a contract by deploying a new one
method.solc_reproduction: the verified input with outputSelection narrowed to the target, compiled by the solc linux-amd64 build of its version; immutable ranges zeroed on both sides. exact: equal; sans-cbor: equal once the trailing CBOR metadata is removed from both
method.source_sets: one compilation from Blockscout's verified record, else Sourcify's; a subject without its own record joins the set whose compiled runtime best equals its code, else its creator's set compiled with every contract selected, else a build of the centrifuge/protocol commit a search of its history finds
method.subject_set: the seed closed over V3's wiring events (Rely, Deny, File, the managers, dependencies, valuations and the factories' deploy logs), each share token's hook and each subject's EIP-1967 slot; a named contract is a subject when Centrifuge wrote it and V3 runs it, and is excluded with its class otherwise; see c_registry.py
